question:
[MCQ] Based on the video clip, what probe orientation is being used at the start of the scan, and what is the acquisition objective?
A. Longitudinal (sagittal) plane; start at the midline to obtain a standard 2D survey sweep of the target organ.
B. Transverse plane; center the structure of interest to optimize depth and focus before acquiring representative still images rather than a full-volume sweep.
C. Transverse plane; begin at the superior portion to start a full-volume sweep
D. Oblique plane; begin at the inferior margin to locate the landmark anatomy before sweeping superiorly for partial coverage.
groundtruth: The operator places the probe in a transverse orientation high on the right liver lobe to start the protocol from the superior aspect before sweeping through the liver.

question:

question:
[MCQ] Based on the video clip, what landmark is used to anchor the next specialized sweep, and what is the purpose of using it?
A. The gallbladder neck; to anchor a sweep through the porta hepatis to screen for biliary obstruction
B. A hepatic vein; to follow it centrally to the IVC as a reference for a venous flow assessment sweep
C. The inferior vena cava; to standardize a longitudinal sweep for estimating volume status and right heart filling pressures
D. A portal venous branch; to standardize the starting point for a border-focused sweep
groundtruth: The right portal vein is located as the starting landmark so the operator can initiate a structured lateral border sweep (“scoop shot”) from a consistent reference point.

question:
[MCQ] Based on the video clip, what coverage strategy is demonstrated, and why is it used?
A. Sliding the probe slightly medially with lighter pressure; used to optimize an intercostal window and reduce rib shadowing, not to interrogate the far lateral margin.
B. Cranial-to-caudal sweep along the long axis without leaving the organ; used to assess superior–inferior extent and look for focal lesions rather than to avoid missing edge anatomy.
C. Lateral sweep fully out of the organ with added pressure, then return to the landmark; ensures complete lateral coverage and avoids missed edge anatomy
D. Fanning (rocking) the probe through the organ while keeping it in view; used to sample different insonation angles and reduce anisotropy rather than to ensure lateral edge coverage.
groundtruth: The operator sweeps laterally with firm pressure until fully out of the liver, then sweeps back medially to the IVC, completing coverage of the superior right lobe from the IVC to the lateral edge and back.
